title: Cap. IX Arg. 1 Resp. Minor: not all damned as gospel-contumacious; reprobation's cause lies elsewhere
pass_a_gloss: Let us approach the Minor; which is not true, if it be understood universally. For many are damned, who are least considered by God as contumacious unto the Gospel. Let the infants of the Pagans be an example, who are born children of wrath, and are least reborn in Christ. An example also among adults can be all those to whom neither the Gospel ever shone, nor Christ became known: Nay even that many are damned by the Law alone, and not on account of contempt of the Gospel, Arminius concedes, Examination of the Predestination of Perkins. But there is no reason that we labor further concerning the Minor. For whether men be damned on account of contempt of the Gospel, or on account of contempt of the Law, yet that the same are reprobated has its cause from elsewhere. Finally, we grant that men are reprobated not without consideration of a despised Law, or Gospel, because God cannot reprobate anyone except as guilty of sin: but from preconsideration of future faith in some, and in others preconsideration of future sin, it by no means follows. For many things are foresighted from eternity by God electing or reprobating as future in the elect or reprobate, which do not have the reason of a moving cause unto the act of reprobating or of electing.
pass_b_english: Now the Minor — which is not true if taken universally. Many are damned who are not at all considered by God as contumacious to the Gospel. Example: pagan infants, born children of wrath and not reborn in Christ. Among adults, all those to whom the Gospel never shone nor Christ became known. Arminius even grants that many are damned by the Law alone, not for contempt of the Gospel (Examination of Perkins's Predestination). No need to labor further on the Minor. Whether men are damned for contempt of Gospel or of Law, that the same are reprobated has its cause elsewhere. Finally we grant men are not reprobated without regard to a despised Law or Gospel, because God cannot reprobate anyone except as guilty of sin — but it does not follow from preconsideration of future faith in some and future sin in others. God electing or reprobating foresights from eternity many future things in elect and reprobate that are not moving causes of the act of electing or reprobating.
source_text: Accedamus ad Minorem; quae non est vera, si universaliter intelligatur. Nam multi damnantur, qui ut Evangelio immorigeri minime a Deo considerantur. Exemplo sint infantes Paganorum, qui filii irae nascuntur, et in Christo minime renascuntur. Exemplo etiam esse possunt inter adultos illi omnes, quibus nec Evangelium illuxit unquam, nec Christus innotuit: Quin etiam multos per solam Legem damnari, et non propter Evangelium contemptum, concedit Arminius, Exam. Praedest. Perkins. Sed non est quod ultra laboremus de Minore. Nam sive ob contemptum Evangelii, sive ob contemptum Legis homines damnentur, tamen, quod iidem reprobentur, aliunde causam habet. Denique, damus, homines reprobari non sine consideratione spretæ Legis, aut Evangelii, quia Deus non potest aliquem reprobare, nisi ut peccati reum: sed ex praeconsideratione fidei futurae in aliquibus, et in aliis praeconsideratione peccati futuri, haud consequitur. Multa enim a Deo eligente aut reprobante praevidentur ab aeterno in electis aut reprobatis futura, quae non habent rationem causae motivae ad actum reprobandi vel eligendi.
